summary: Round-7 independent arbitration at source_digest sha256:767b17f6..., re-derived from scratch at this digest and carrying nothing forward from the round-6 record. The round-6 blocking finding is genuinely closed and the fix survives the specific attack the author asked for: the new leg binds the default rule, not merely a parse-nothing path. My own probe of `aw capability report --project demo --skip-issue-inventory` on UNCLASSIFIED_DOCUMENT shows all six capabilities parsing (ids search-core, lexical-search, standard-operational-endpoints, kubernetes-native-deployment, security-hardening, ec-gates-configured; per-item claim_count 1,2,1,1,1,1 = 7), every per-item feature_class absent, and core 0/0 against non_core 6/7 -- so `capabilities` is non-empty, the capabilities.is_empty() fallback at capability.rs:1287 is not what produces those totals, and CapabilityReportItem::effective_feature_class's `.unwrap_or(NonCore)` is the only thing that can place them. Confirmed by mutation rather than by reading: my harness flipped that default to Core, rebuilt, and the case went RED inside assert_unclassified_defaults_to_non_core, which is the only leg that can see it since every other document the fixture runs declares its own class. I re-derived three more anchored mutations of src/cli/capability.rs independently and all were caught by this case: removing the `if !declares_any_class { return findings; }` early return at capability.rs:10048 (CAUGHT -- so the silence half of the new assertion is discriminating, not decorative), and inverting migration_feature_class (CAUGHT at assert_migration_derives_the_split, so the round-5 finding stays closed). capability.rs was restored in a finally block and `git diff --quiet` confirms it is byte-identical to HEAD, with the binary rebuilt from the restored source. I also verified a non-obvious risk the new call introduces: inserting a `capability report` run before `capability migrate` does not perturb the migration leg's input -- report is read-only on cap_path (sha256 of the document identical before and after). The load-bearing fixture facts hold: the four NON_CORE_IDS are all real baseline_caps entries in src/cli/doc_mirror.rs while observability, search-core and lexical-search are not, so the conflict falsifier and the preservation leg are discriminating rather than tautological. The disclosure the author added is materially correct on delegation -- `cargo test -p agentic-workflow --lib markdown_capability_tables` selects 21 tests including reject_a_document_missing_a_feature_root, reject_an_unknown_feature_root and reject_a_multiply_classified_capability, so the three disclosed rules do have a declared home -- and its two worked examples reproduce exactly (5 blockers and 2 blockers respectively). Structural gates re-run clean at this digest: aw ec check clean with expected_case_count == case_count == 66 and stale false, inventory_parity self-consistent at 66 cases / 74 retained Rust invariants / behavior 50 efficiency 8 stability 8, claim_reconciliation --verify status clean with cargo_delegating_command_count 0 and rust_invariant_case_count 0 (never run with --write), migration_reconciliation verify --baseline (unmatched 0, duplicate 0) / --policy pass / --guidance clean / --retired-tree clean; verify --projections is red only on the stale lock, and the stale set is exactly this change (case capability-control-plane-markdown-capability-schema, pyproject.toml and capability_manual.py changed, oracles/lumen_feature_class_reference.py added), so no other EC IR entry drifted. The gate reproduces at 12 assertions, exit 0, assertions_digest sha256:e30e1ed9018e51e0776b81681b9db0f10813aee08adecae5ac430d563d123d0b, matching the committed evidence file byte-for-byte, and fails closed by construction: run_aw raises on a non-zero exit and final_json raises `command emitted no JSON`, so an exit-0 no-output binary reddens the case at its first call, and an AssertionError from verify() propagates out of runner.py as a non-zero exit. git confirms no Rust product source in either 1e9367fc0f or 82924c4e88 -- `git diff --name-only 1e9367fc0f~1 82924c4e88` lists only external-contracts/pyproject.toml, src/migration_clusters/capability_manual.py and src/oracles/lumen_feature_class_reference.py, and zero *.rs paths. Two defects block acceptance. First, the fourth instance of the round-5/round-6 class does exist, and it is the other branch of the very rule this round closed: a legacy-table document is attributed wholly to non-core by the capabilities.is_empty() fallback at capability.rs:1287-1292, no EC case runs that shape, and neutering the fallback leaves this case green while reddening exactly one crate-internal test that no declared filter selects -- observable at the CLI as core 0 / non_core 0 against capability_count 3, three capabilities in neither class. Second, the new disclosure overstates itself on one of its three rules: a capability under both roots is a single-message falsifier (one bare `#### Search Core` heading under the Non-Core root yields exactly one document blocker), so the docstring's generalization that none of the three can be added as a single-message falsifier is false as written. This record is agent-backed arbitration input for the human batch audit, not human acceptance evidence, and it authorizes only source_digest sha256:767b17f6983a67461ed850f92376a04da2e352653000c5761e811d428ec30add.
findings: capability-control-plane-markdown-capability-schema: the new leg does bind the default rule, but only on the branch where capability sections parse; the second branch of the same stated rule -- a legacy-table document, whose rows are attributed wholly to non-core by CapabilityReport::apply_feature_class_totals at apps/agentic-workflow/src/cli/capability.rs:1287-1292 (`if self.capabilities.is_empty() { self.non_core_capability_count = self.capability_count; ... }`) -- is exercised by no EC case and by no declared gate. This is the fourth instance of the round-5/round-6 defect class. Independently reproduced with my own harness at this digest: neutering that block to `if false` leaves this case GREEN (exit 0, 12 assertions, assertions_digest unchanged at sha256:e30e1ed9018e51e0776b81681b9db0f10813aee08adecae5ac430d563d123d0b) while a full `cargo test -p agentic-workflow --lib` run goes from 0 baseline failures to exactly one failure, cli::capability::tests::report_attributes_legacy_rows_to_non_core_rather_than_dropping_them, which no one of the 256 `cargo test -p agentic-workflow --lib <filter>` filters declared in apps/agentic-workflow/CAPABILITIES.md selects, and which is referenced nowhere in the EC inventory. The behavior is externally observable, not a crate-internal invariant: on a real legacy-table document (a `## Capabilities` table with Capability / Current State / Gaps / Active WI / Evidence columns and three rows, which is_legacy_only() at capability.rs:877-879 routes to capability_count = legacy_rows.len() at capability.rs:6267-6274) `aw capability report --project demo --skip-issue-inventory` reports core_capability_count 0 / non_core_capability_count 3 / capability_count 3 at HEAD and core 0 / non_core 0 / capability_count 3 under the mutation -- three capabilities in neither class, which is precisely the totality this case's assertion 4 (`each per-class pair summing to its retained total`) and new assertion 9 (`attributed wholly to non-core, capabilities and claims alike`) claim. Revision: add a LEGACY_TABLE_DOCUMENT constant to apps/agentic-workflow/external-contracts/src/oracles/lumen_feature_class_reference.py holding a `## Capabilities` legacy table with the Capability / Current State / Gaps / Active WI / Evidence header and a fixed set of rows built from the same real Lumen ids; report it once in _lumen_feature_class_snapshot() in src/migration_clusters/capability_manual.py via the existing _lumen_report helper; and add an assert_legacy_rows_are_attributed_to_non_core(report) helper that pins the live projection: capabilities == [] with capability_count equal to the row count (so the shape under test is asserted, not assumed), core_capability_count == 0 and core_claim_count == 0, non_core_capability_count == capability_count and non_core_claim_count == claim_count, non_core_verified_count == verified_count, and document_blockers(report) == [the exact `legacy capability table detected; migrate rows to canonical field-style capability contracts under ## Capabilities` message] so the leg also pins that this shape is diagnosed rather than silently accepted. Then add the matching assertion string to the case's returned list in capability_manual.py and extend the pyproject oracle clause to say that a legacy-only document's rows are attributed to non-core in full rather than dropping out of both classes.

capability-control-plane-markdown-capability-schema: the new disclosure in the module docstring of apps/agentic-workflow/external-contracts/src/oracles/lumen_feature_class_reference.py:25-33 states a falsehood about one of the three rules it discloses. Its two named justifications are both accurate and I verified them live -- deleting `### Non-Core Features` from REFERENCE_DOCUMENT yields exactly 5 document blockers (one missing `### Non-Core Features` root plus one field/root contradiction per stranded baseline: standard-operational-endpoints, kubernetes-native-deployment, security-hardening, ec-gates-configured), and renaming it to `### Extra Features` yields exactly 2 (missing `### Non-Core Features` root plus unknown feature root `Extra Features`). But the sentence generalizes over all three -- `They cannot be added as single-message falsifiers` -- and that is false for the third, a capability nested under both roots. Appending the single line `#### Search Core` inside the Non-Core root of REFERENCE_DOCUMENT yields document_blockers(report) == ['capability `search-core` is classified under both `Core Features` and `Non-Core Features`; keep exactly one root'] -- one message, all six capabilities still parsing, structurally identical to the three falsifiers the fixture already carries. scan_feature_roots at capability.rs:9998-10008 records root membership from headings alone, so no second section body and no co-occurring-set assertion is needed. (The full-section duplication that does produce a different shape collapses the document to `no capability sections found`, which is a different defect and not this rule.) The claim being false matters because it is the artifact's own statement of why a cheap falsifier was omitted, and the next reader will trust it. Revision: either promote the both-roots rule to a real falsifier -- a MULTIPLY_CLASSIFIED_DOCUMENT constant appending the bare `#### Search Core` heading under the Non-Core root plus an assert_capability_under_both_roots_is_rejected(report) helper asserting that exact single message, in the same shape as assert_duplicate_root_is_rejected -- or narrow the docstring to say that missing root and unknown root are the two that cannot be single-message falsifiers, and state the actual reason the both-roots rule is left out.
